correctness.rationale: The monotone equation q_i(a_i+q_i)=kappa b_i^2 and sum q_i^2/b_i^2=1 has exactly one positive solution. Expanding the submitted exact sum-of-squares identity proves every box-plus-ellipsoid point satisfies sum x_i^2/[d(a_i+q_i)^2]<=1; positive a_i forces equality only at the 2^d coordinate-sign contacts. Rescaling these contacts gives mean 0 and covariance I/d. Averaging an arbitrary translated/rotated enclosing ellipsoid inequality and using trace>=d*(det)^(1/d) proves it cannot have lower volume; equality forces the identity shape and zero center. My independently written rational-arithmetic checker verified the identity for 1,088 exact parameter/point cases, not a replacement for the universal proof.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge PASS, qualified. Classical Loewner/John contact criteria characterize optimality but do not calculate this anisotropic rounded-box family. Halder (2018) computes parameterized MVOE outer approximations for sums of ellipsoids, not the globally optimal enclosing ellipsoid of a nondegenerate box plus a coaxial ellipsoid with all contacts. Courteaux et al. (2025) treat the exact summand type but construct bounding-box-based implicit approximations; the inspected article does not entail the scalar optimum. Resultary hits are Loewner ellipsoids of unrelated rank-selected polytopes/permutohedra, not this set. The general optimality criterion alone is not a prior expression of the new shape without the substantial identity and contact construction.
residual_risks: An older specialized treatment of Loewner ellipsoids of axis-aligned parallel-body sums might already contain an equivalent scalar formula despite absence in checked sources.
Only coaxial strictly positive widths are proved; arbitrary relative rotations, vanishing widths, and other rounding norms are excluded.
